overall_summary: Deduplication reveals 47 distinct Shorts. Across the library, content breaks into two distinct tiers: first-person hypothetical survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic horror/exoplanet mysteries consistently capture the highest engagement (800–1,050+ views, 3.5%+ like ratios, and active comment threads). Conversely, repetitive neurology trivia, duplicate re-uploads of earworm/fake-memory facts, and passive star facts suffer acute fatigue, often plateauing below 50 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Survival Micro-Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos using this immersive simulation frame achieved peak metrics: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes, 2 comments), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (824 views, 15 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Maintain the visceral first-person simulator POV ('You step out of your capsule...') to instantly lock viewer retention through sensory survival stakes.

winning_patterns.pattern: Visceral Cosmic Extremes & Forbidden Exoplanet Physics
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' hit 1,031 views with 36 likes and 2 comments, and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' earned 725 views and 25 likes, outperforming generic space trivia by over 10x.
winning_patterns.action: Pair bizarre astrophysical phenomena with tangible sensory imagery (crushing pressure, razor-sharp rains, total sensory deprivation).

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles centered on 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' and earworms generated as low as 5, 10, 17, and 53 views across repeated attempts, with near-zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Cease recycling identical psychology scripts and stale neuro-trivia without narrative or dramatic stakes.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' (11 views, 0 likes) and 'The Eyeball Planet That Could Harbor Life!' (49 views, 0 likes) stalled due to weak emotional tension and non-urgent hooks.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate static declarative facts; replace passive explanations with dynamic what-if consequences and high-stakes cinematic tension.

next_video.opening_direction: Start mid-descent: 'If you dropped out of hyperspace onto exoplanet TOI-1452 b, you wouldn't see a single grain of land—just a pitch-black ocean 100 times deeper than Earth's.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that diving to the seabed wouldn't hit rock; the immense atmospheric pressure forces water into exotic 'Ice VII'—solid ice that burns at hundreds of degrees without melting.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If You Fell Into' simulation architecture while targeting a completely unaddressed, claustrophobic exoplanet mystery (super-Earth water worlds) rather than re-treading diamond or ice planets.
